questions.stem: A triglyceride is formed from one glycerol and three fatty acids. What type of reaction joins them, and what is the bond called?
questions.explanation: Triglycerides are formed by condensation reactions between glycerol and three fatty acids, forming three ester bonds and releasing three molecules of water. Glycosidic bonds are found in carbohydrates and peptide bonds in proteins.

questions.stem: Arctic animals like polar bears have a thick layer of body fat under their skin. Which TWO functions does this fat layer serve?

options.text: Protection from UV light and hormone production

questions.explanation: Fat (adipose tissue) serves as a long-term energy store, containing twice as much energy per gram as carbohydrates. It also acts as an excellent thermal insulator, reducing heat loss to the cold environment. This is critical for polar bears surviving in arctic conditions where food can be scarce and temperatures are extremely low.

questions.stem: A food sample is shaken with ethanol, then the ethanol is poured into water. A white cloudy emulsion forms. What does this positive result indicate?
questions.explanation: This describes the emulsion test for lipids. Lipids dissolve in ethanol but not in water. When the ethanol solution is added to water, the lipids come out of solution as tiny droplets, scattering light and producing a white cloudy emulsion. A clear solution means lipids are absent.

questions.stem: Olive oil is liquid at room temperature while butter is solid. What structural difference in their fatty acids explains this?

options.text: Olive oil has shorter fatty acid chains
Olive oil contains unsaturated fatty acids with double bonds that create kinks, preventing close packing
Butter contains more glycerol than olive oil
Olive oil has more ester bonds

questions.explanation: Unsaturated fatty acids (found in olive oil) have C=C double bonds that create kinks in the hydrocarbon chains. These kinks prevent the molecules from packing closely together, so the fat is liquid at room temperature (an oil). Saturated fatty acids (in butter) have no double bonds, pack tightly, and are solid at room temperature.

questions.stem: Phospholipids form the basis of cell membranes. They have a hydrophilic head and hydrophobic tails. How do they arrange themselves in water to form a membrane?

options.text: In a single layer with tails facing the water
In a bilayer with hydrophilic heads facing outward toward water and hydrophobic tails facing inward
In a bilayer with hydrophobic tails facing outward

questions.explanation: Phospholipids spontaneously form a bilayer in water. The hydrophilic (water-loving) heads face outward, interacting with the aqueous environment inside and outside the cell. The hydrophobic (water-fearing) tails face inward, away from water, creating a barrier that controls what enters and leaves the cell.
